title: Religious symbols
examples: What does the dharma wheel mean?

explain.say: A symbol is a picture that carries a big meaning in a small shape. Each faith has symbols its followers recognise at a glance: Om, the cross, the Star of David, the crescent and star, the dharma wheel and the khanda.

Om, also written Aum, is the sacred sound of Hinduism, chanted at the start of prayers. Many Hindus see it as the sound of ultimate reality, Brahman. The cross is the main Christian symbol, recalling Jesus's death and, for Christians, his resurrection.

a: A sacred sound, A, U, M
Chanted at the start of prayers
b: Points to belief in the resurrection
Crucifix: a cross with the figure of Jesus

explain.say: The six-pointed Star of David, the Magen David, is a widely used Jewish symbol, alongside the older seven-branched menorah. The crescent and star is linked with Islam and appears on many flags, though many Muslims say Islam has no official symbol.

a: Magen David, the Shield of David
The menorah is an even older symbol
b: Seen on many flags and mosques
Arabic calligraphy is also widely used

explain.say: The dharma wheel, the dharmachakra, stands for the Buddha's teaching. Its eight spokes are the Noble Eightfold Path, and the Buddha's first sermon is called setting the wheel of dharma in motion.

draw.text: Eight spokes: the Noble Eightfold Path.

explain.say: The khanda is the Sikh emblem. A double-edged sword in the centre stands for divine truth, the circle for one God without beginning or end, and two curved swords for spiritual and worldly responsibility.

items: Two kirpans: spiritual and worldly power

draw.text: Ik Onkar, One Creator, opens the Sikh scripture.

explain.say: Here they are together. Remember that a symbol's meaning comes from the people who use it, so the best way to learn it is to ask what it means to them.

Cross | Christian | Jesus's death and resurrection
Star of David | Jewish | Shield of David, Jewish identity
Crescent and star | Islam | Widely linked to Islam
Dharma wheel | Buddhist | The Buddha's teaching
Khanda | Sikh | One God, truth, justice

faq.q: What does the dharma wheel mean?
faq.a: The dharma wheel, or dharmachakra, stands for the Buddha's teaching, the dharma. Its eight spokes represent the Noble Eightfold Path, and the round wheel can suggest the cycle of life and the completeness of the teaching. The Buddha's first sermon at Sarnath is called turning the wheel of dharma.
asks: why does the dharma wheel have eight spokes

faq.a: The khanda is the emblem of Sikhism. In the middle is a double-edged sword, also called a khanda, for divine truth; around it a circle, the chakkar, for one God without beginning or end; and on each side a curved sword, a kirpan, for spiritual and worldly responsibility.
asks: what does the Sikh flag show

faq.a: Om, or Aum, is a sacred sound in Hinduism, chanted at the beginning and end of prayers and meditation. Many Hindus understand it as the sound of Brahman, ultimate reality, and its three sounds A, U and M are given many meanings. It is also used in Buddhism and Jainism.

faq.q: What does the cross mean to Christians?
faq.a: The cross reminds Christians that Jesus died by crucifixion, which they believe was for the sake of the world, and that he rose again. A crucifix shows the figure of Jesus on the cross and is common in Catholic and Orthodox churches; many Protestant churches use an empty cross to point to the resurrection.
asks: why is the cross a Christian symbol

faq.q: What is the Star of David?
faq.a: The Star of David, Magen David in Hebrew, meaning Shield of David, is a six-pointed star made of two triangles. It became a widely used symbol of Jewish identity in recent centuries and appears on the flag of Israel. The seven-branched menorah is an even older Jewish symbol.

faq.q: Is the crescent and star the symbol of Islam?
faq.a: The crescent and star is widely linked with Islam and appears on the flags of several Muslim-majority countries, such as Turkey and Pakistan. It became popular through the Ottoman Empire. Many Muslims say Islam has no official symbol, and Arabic calligraphy of God's name is also widely used.
asks: why is there a moon on mosques

faq.a: Ik Onkar means there is one Creator, or one God. It is the first phrase of the Guru Granth Sahib, the Sikh scripture, and is written with the numeral one followed by a curving letter. It is one of the most important Sikh symbols.
asks: first words of the Guru Granth Sahib

faq.q: What does the lotus flower mean?
faq.a: In Buddhism and Hinduism the lotus stands for purity and spiritual awakening, because it grows from muddy water yet blooms clean and beautiful above it. The Buddha and Hindu deities such as Lakshmi are often shown seated on a lotus.

faq.q: What does the yin-yang symbol mean?
faq.a: The yin-yang symbol comes from Chinese thought and is important in Daoism. Its dark and light halves, each with a dot of the other, show that opposites such as dark and light or rest and movement depend on each other and stay in balance.

faq.q: Why is the swastika a Hindu symbol?
faq.a: In Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism the swastika is an ancient sign of good fortune and well-being, used for thousands of years; the word comes from Sanskrit for well-being. In the 20th century the Nazis misused a version of it, so in many countries it now causes great pain, and its religious meaning needs careful explanation.
asks: what does the swastika mean in Hinduism

faq.a: Almost all do, but they use them differently. Some faiths fill their buildings with images, while others, like many mosques, avoid pictures of living beings and use patterns and calligraphy instead. Humanists, who are not religious, often use the Happy Human figure.
asks: does every religion have a symbol

faq.a: The Jain emblem shows a raised palm with a wheel on it, standing for ahimsa, non-violence, with the word ahimsa written inside. Above it are three dots and a crescent, standing for the Jain path and liberation.

faq.q: Why are symbols important in religion?
faq.a: Symbols let people express big ideas, like God, truth or the path to peace, in a simple shape that everyone can see. They help people remember beliefs, show they belong to a community, and focus their minds in prayer.
asks: what is the point of a religious symbol

facts: The eight spokes of the dharma wheel stand for the Noble Eightfold Path.
The khanda combines a double-edged sword, a circle called the chakkar, and two curved kirpans.
Magen David, the Hebrew name of the Star of David, means Shield of David.
Ik Onkar, meaning one Creator, is the opening phrase of the Guru Granth Sahib.
Om, or Aum, is chanted at the start of Hindu prayers and is also used in Buddhism and Jainism.
